title: Relative module flatness is detected on a flat source cover
statement: Let $f:Y\to S$ and $h:X\to Y$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $\mathcal G$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $x\in X$ and put $y=h(x)$. If $h$ is flat at $x$ [def-weil-flat-morphism], then $\mathcal G$ is flat over $S$ at $y$ if and only if $h^*\mathcal G$ is flat over $S$ at $x$, where the two structure maps are $f$ and $fh$ respectively [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over], [def-pc-module-pullback]. Consequently, for any jointly surjective family of flat morphisms $h_i:X_i\to Y$, the module $\mathcal G$ is flat over $S$ if and only if every $h_i^*\mathcal G$ is flat over $S$; jointly surjective means every point of $Y$ has a preimage in some $X_i$. No quasi-compactness, finite-presentation, or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.
